parsed.rationale: Both `MainActorNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/MainActorMessage.swift:43) and `AsyncNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift:39) are production interfaces in the same `Core` package sharing two identical members: `makeNotification:(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification` and `name:Notification.Name`. The only structural difference is the concurrency annotation on `makeMessage`: `sending Notification` in `MainActorNotificationMessage` vs plain `Notification` in `AsyncNotificationMessage`. This suggests a common base protocol should capture the shared contract, with each child protocol refining `makeMessage` according to its concurrency semantics. No restraint markers are present on either record, making consolidation safe. The alternative of extracting a new parent protocol is the most idiomatic Swift approach here; however, since `AsyncNotificationMessage` already exists in the cluster, it is the natural candidate to serve as the parent (or to be renamed to a base), with `MainActorNotificationMessage` inheriting and narrowing `makeMessage` to the `sending`/`@MainActor` variant.
